findings.claim: §6 claims 'WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 sets [require_code_owner_reviews: true] on SCP main (it is part of the standard required-status-check configuration applied at 020D2)', but this flag does not appear in any plan document other than this assertion. The 020D2 slice spec at plan line 177 enumerates four branch-protection flags and omits require_code_owner_reviews: true. A Codex executor following the 020D2 slice spec would not set this flag, leaving CODEOWNERS unenforced on main — contrary to §6's claim of BYPASS-005 closure from 020D2 onward.
findings.evidence: §6 manifest-integrity block (plan lines 553–564): 'CODEOWNERS alone does not block PRs — branch-protection must also set require_code_owner_reviews: true for the rule to be enforced gate-side. WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 sets this on SCP main (it is part of the standard required-status-check configuration applied at 020D2), so from 020D2 onward any change to the manifest requires CODEOWNERS approval before merge.' 020D2 slice description (plan line 177): 'scp/policy-check required with enforce_admins=true; required_approving_review_count=1; dismiss_stale_reviews: true; require_review_from_non_author=false' — require_code_owner_reviews absent. grep of docs/plans/ for 'require_code_owner_reviews': exactly one match — plan line 555, the §6 claim itself. R4 reviewer evidence confirmed zero matches across all plan documents in v0.4; v0.5 adds one match (the self-referential assertion). WP-SCP-020 is not separately read in this review, but it falls within docs/plans/ and the grep covers it.
findings.impact: If the 020D2 Codex executor follows the slice spec and require_code_owner_reviews: true is not in that spec, CODEOWNERS enforcement on SCP main never activates. The acc-pin-manifest.json remains unprotected by CODEOWNERS gate enforcement for the lifetime of the chain. §6 documents this as a closed BYPASS-005 and may cause the operator to treat manifest integrity as enforced when it is not, relaxing vigilance prematurely on the highest-security artefact in the dispatch protocol.
findings.mitigation: Option A (preferred): add 'require_code_owner_reviews: true' explicitly to the 020D2 slice description at plan line 177 (or in WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 if that is the authoritative spec source), then confirm the §6 claim is now backed by the slice spec. Option B: change the §6 parenthetical from 'WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 sets this on SCP main' to 'require_code_owner_reviews: true must be added to the 020D2 branch-protection API call; this flag should be specified in WP-SCP-020 §4 020D2 so the Codex executor sets it' and update the BYPASS-005 closure claim to reflect that enforcement is contingent on that spec addition.

findings.claim: §4.1 verify_commands guidance does not cross-reference §8 R-022-13 for the 020J-specific API verify commands. The §9 AC added in v0.5 references §8 R-022-13 for the post-execution evidence requirement, but §4.1 is the primary specification consulted by an orchestrator building a dispatch package. An orchestrator applying §4.1 verify_commands rules mechanically for 020J could omit the two gh-api state checks if it does not also consult §8.
findings.evidence: §4.1 verify_commands guidance (plan lines 261–264): 'Always includes pytest for the relevant test path; for workflow slices includes actionlint; for Rego slices includes conftest verify + opa test.' No mention of 020J-specific API verify commands or a pointer to §8 R-022-13. §9 AC (plan lines 741–744): 'Slice 020J's both API-state verify_commands per §8 R-022-13 passed at slice-merge time...' — references §8 only at the evidence-verification stage, not at the dispatch-package-build stage. R4 F-R4-002 mitigation explicitly requested: 'cross-reference §8 R-022-13 from §4.1's verify_commands guidance (e.g. for the 020J tag-protection + signed-commits slice, verify_commands are specified in §8 R-022-13).' This cross-reference was not added to §4.1.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to §4.1 verify_commands: 'For the 020J tag-protection + signed-commits slice, verify_commands are specified in §8 R-022-13 (two gh-api state checks: tag-protection match and required_signatures.enabled=true).' Single-line addition; no content change.

findings.claim: scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh line 51 defines an unused variable SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL (singular) that is never read by the script. The active operator-identity override mechanism uses SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS (plural), consumed at line 120 via ${SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS:-${SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS_DEFAULT}}. An operator who reads line 51 and sets SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL=their@email.com in the environment gains no effect on gate verification — the dead variable silently consumes the value without passing it to verify_gate_commit_author.
findings.evidence: gate_check.sh line 51: SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL="${SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL:-jrnb2024}" — defined. grep of gate_check.sh for 'SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL[^S]' returns: line 51 (definition), line 54 (comment). grep for 'SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS' (plural) returns: line 54 (comment), line 56 (SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS_DEFAULT definition), line 102 (docstring), line 110 (example), line 120 (active read). The singular variable at line 51 is never referenced downstream; verify_gate_commit_author reads only ${SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS:-${SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS_DEFAULT}}.
findings.mitigation: Remove line 51 (the SCP_OPERATOR_EMAIL singular definition). The plural SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS env-var at line 120 is the correct override interface. Optionally add 'Override: export SCP_OPERATOR_EMAILS=email1:email2' to the usage() block so operators can discover the correct env-var name.
